description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs carries 15 load-bearing #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)] annotations after JMAP-x2gd.105 cleaned up the 2 dead ones. Each suppresses a default-on clippy warning that the function's Err-variant is at least 200 bytes (the lint threshold is 128 bytes).

Affected return shapes:
- Result<Vec<OpResult>, BackendSetError<MemoryError>>
- Result<Option<jmap_chat_types::Space>, BackendSetError<MemoryError>>
- Result<Option<Id>, SetError>
- Result<(), SetError>

The clippy lint suggests two fixes:
  (a) Box<BackendSetError<E>> and Box<SetError> at the return type.
  (b) Shrink SetError itself (currently 8 typed Option fields + extras Map).

Both are workspace-architectural: SetError and BackendSetError live in jmap-server (foundation), and the type is used across all 8 extension-server crates plus their MemoryBackends. Any change here propagates to: jmap-server (canonical), jmap-mail-server (canonical extension), jmap-chat-server, jmap-calendars-server, jmap-tasks-server, jmap-contacts-server, jmap-filenode-server, jmap-metadata-server, jmap-sharing-server.

Why chat-server fires but mail-server does not: chat-server has extensive inherent-method and free-function pre-validation helpers around Space mutations (apply_space_patch_impl + 12 apply_* variants + validate_space_patch_ops + check_count_caps' callees). Mail-server's MemoryBackend uses trait-impl methods almost exclusively; clippy's result_large_err lint allow-list-by-default appears to skip trait-impl return types.

Engineering basis for action:
- 15 per-fn allow attributes are noise. Future maintainers will read them as suppressing a non-firing lint (per JMAP-x2gd.105's premise — which was wrong) and either delete them prematurely (breaking the workspace gate) or assume each fn is intentionally large (false).
- Box<SetError> on the Err arm shrinks the Result from ~208 bytes to 16 bytes (pointer + tag). On the hot success path (Ok), 16 bytes vs 208 bytes is a measurable stack-frame and copy difference.
- All ergonomic constructors (SetError::new, with_description, etc.) can grow Box-returning siblings or callers can wrap at the return site.

Workspace-canonical implication:
- Decide between (a) Box at the return type or (b) shrink SetError.
- Land on jmap-server canonical first; propagate to all extension-server siblings in the same pass.
- After the propagation, every #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)] across all extension-server crates can be deleted (sibling sweep).

Alternatives considered and rejected here:
- Move SetError to a Box<SetError> only in the Err arm via thiserror-style separation: workspace policy is no thiserror, no error-helper crates.
- Crate-level #[allow] on chat-server: weakens the workspace clippy gate intent (each gate is per-warning, the lint should fire when a new big Err is added).

Pre-cursor: JMAP-x2gd.105 (closed 2026-05-17). My outcome there fixed 2 dead allows; this bead carries the canonical workspace decision the remaining 15 require.
title: Box-or-shrink SetError / BackendSetError: 15 result_large_err allows in chat-server MemoryBackend signal canonical-cleanup opportunity
